resumen: Significado: el sentido de un phrasal verb no siempre se deduce de sus partes: give up = dejar, turn down = rechazar, break down = averiarse.
Separables (look up, turn down, bring up, put off, let down): el sustantivo puede ir antes o después de la partícula, pero el pronombre va siempre en medio: turn it down, nunca turn down it.
Inseparables (look after, come across, get over): el objeto, también si es pronombre, va después de la partícula: She looks after them.
De tres partes (run out of, put up with, get on with, cut down on, live up to): no se separan y la preposición final es obligatoria: We've run out of milk.
look forward to + -ing, porque to es preposición: I'm looking forward to seeing you.
Pares que se confunden: put off (aplazar) / call off (cancelar); come across (encontrar por casualidad) / come up with (idear); take over (asumir el mando) / take after (parecerse a).
Sin objeto: break down, fall through, carry on o grow up no llevan objeto directo: The deal fell through.

preguntas.q: Could you ___ my cat while I'm on holiday next week?
preguntas.x: Look after = «cuidar» a una persona o un animal. Look for es «buscar» y look into «investigar», así que no encajan con cuidar al gato mientras estás fuera.

preguntas.q: We're really looking forward ___ you at the graduation ceremony.
preguntas.x: En look forward to («tener muchas ganas de»), to es una preposición, así que va seguida de -ing o de un sustantivo: looking forward to seeing you. To see es el error más frecuente.

preguntas.q: My dad ___ smoking ten years ago, and he feels much healthier now.
preguntas.x: Give up + -ing = «dejar (un hábito)». Give in es «ceder, rendirse» y give away «regalar»; ninguno significa abandonar una costumbre.

preguntas.q: I'll ring the museum to ___ what time it opens on Sunday.
preguntas.x: Find out = «averiguar, enterarse de» un dato. Turn out es «resultar», look out «tener cuidado» y make up «inventar»; ninguno significa conseguir información.

preguntas.q: We've ___ milk, so I'll pop to the corner shop before breakfast.
preguntas.x: Run out of + sustantivo = «quedarse sin»: We've run out of milk. Sin of el verbo no lleva objeto (The milk has run out), y run over es «atropellar».

preguntas.q: Don't worry, the meeting hasn't been ___ altogether; it's just been ___ until Friday.
preguntas.x: Call off = «cancelar» (altogether, del todo) y put off = «aplazar» (until Friday). Si se invierten, la frase pierde la lógica: algo no se cancela «hasta el viernes».

preguntas.q: Sorry for interrupting. Please ___ with your presentation.
preguntas.x: Carry on (with something) = «continuar». Carry out es «llevar a cabo» y va con objeto directo, sin with (carry out a survey).

preguntas.q: I ___ well with my ex now, but it took me months to ___ the break-up.
preguntas.x: Get on (well) with someone = «llevarse bien con alguien» y get over something = «superar» una ruptura o una enfermedad. Get by es «arreglárselas» y get off «bajarse (de un vehículo)»; ninguno significa superar.

preguntas.q: While searching online, I ___ an interesting article, and it helped me ___ an idea for my essay.
preguntas.x: Come across = «encontrar por casualidad» y come up with = «idear, ocurrírsele a uno» (una idea, un plan). Come up sin with significa «surgir» y no lleva objeto.

preguntas.q: My grandparents ___ in Quetzaltenango while my parents were working abroad.
preguntas.x: Bring someone up = «criar». Es separable y, con pronombre, este va en medio: brought me up, nunca brought up me. Grow up («crecer») no lleva objeto, así que grew me up es incorrecto.

preguntas.q: She ___ the job offer because the salary was too low.
preguntas.x: Turn down = «rechazar» (una oferta, una invitación). Turn off es «apagar» y turn up «subir el volumen» o «aparecer».

preguntas.q: Sorry I'm late: the bus ___ on the motorway and we had to wait for another one.
preguntas.x: Break down = «averiarse» (un vehículo, una máquina). Break out es «estallar» (una guerra, un incendio) y break in «entrar a la fuerza».

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: My aunt looks after the twins when I'm at work.
d: I didn't know the word, so I looked up it.
The match was on Friday, but they put off it.
Those old photos? I came them across in a drawer.
preguntas.x: Con los separables (look up, put off) el pronombre va entre el verbo y la partícula: looked it up, put it off. Los inseparables (look after, come across) nunca se dividen: came across them.

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “My cousin founded her own design company in 2020.”
preguntas.a: My cousin set up her own design company in 2020.
d: My cousin took over her own design company in 2020.
My cousin set off her own design company in 2020.
My cousin put up her own design company in 2020.
preguntas.x: Set up = «fundar, montar» un negocio. Take over también se usa con empresas, pero significa «tomar el control» de una que ya existe, no crearla; set off es «ponerse en camino».

preguntas.q: When the founder retired, his daughter ___ from him as CEO.
preguntas.x: Take over (from someone) = «relevar a alguien, asumir el mando». Take after significa «parecerse a un familiar» (She takes after her father), y take on («contratar, asumir una tarea») no se construye con from him.

preguntas.q: I promised Ana I'd help her move house on Saturday, so I can't ___ now.
preguntas.x: Let someone down = «fallarle a alguien, decepcionarlo». Es separable y el pronombre va en medio (let her down); let her off significa «perdonarle un castigo».

preguntas.q: Choose the sentence that means the same as: “I can't tolerate the noise from my neighbours any longer.”
preguntas.a: I can't put up with the noise from my neighbours any longer.
d: I can't put up the noise from my neighbours any longer.
I can't get over the noise from my neighbours any longer.
I can't put off the noise from my neighbours any longer.
preguntas.x: Put up with = «aguantar, tolerar». Sin with, put up significa «colgar» o «alojar», y can't get over something expresa asombro («no me lo puedo creer»), no falta de tolerancia.

preguntas.q: My doctor told me to ___ sugar, so now I have one biscuit a day instead of five.
preguntas.x: Cut down on = «reducir el consumo de» algo; pasar de cinco galletas a una es reducir, no eliminar. Cut off es «cortar (un suministro)» o «aislar», y cut out of y cut down with no funcionan con este sentido.

preguntas.q: Sadly, the new phone didn't ___ the expectations created by its advertising campaign.
preguntas.x: Live up to + expectativas o fama = «estar a la altura de». Necesita to antes del objeto; live on es «vivir de» (live on a small salary) y come up with, «idear».

preguntas.q: Which sentence is correct?
preguntas.a: Our plans to visit Tikal fell through at the last minute.
d: Can you point out me where the exit is?
The police have ruled out to arrest anyone.
I can't work out him: he never says what he thinks.
preguntas.x: Fall through = «venirse abajo, no concretarse» (un plan). En las otras se dice point out to me («señalarme»), rule out + sustantivo o -ing (ruled out arresting, «descartaron») y work him out («entenderlo»), con el pronombre en medio.
